antiquity.name: Ancient World
antiquity.summary: Gods, rulers and the ideal body
antiquity.description: From Egypt to Greece and Rome, artists carve rulers, gods and athletes meant to last forever. Their search for the ideal body became the model for centuries of Western art.

gothic.name: Gothic & Proto-Renaissance
gothic.summary: Gold grounds and the first real emotions
gothic.description: In churches and chapels, painters still work on gold, but their figures begin to weep, to turn, to have weight. Storytelling in pictures is being reinvented.

early_netherlandish.name: Early Netherlandish
early_netherlandish.description: In Flanders, painters perfect oil paint and use it to describe everything: fur, glass, a tear, a reflection. Sacred scenes move into rooms that look like real homes.

renaissance.name: Italian Renaissance
renaissance.summary: Perspective and a return to antiquity
renaissance.description: In Italy, then across Europe, artists rediscover antiquity, study the human body and invent perspective. The painting becomes a window onto the world.

northern_renaissance.name: Northern Renaissance
northern_renaissance.summary: Sharp lines, prints and strange visions
northern_renaissance.description: North of the Alps, artists mix Italian ideas with a love of detail and of everyday life. Printmaking spreads their images across Europe.

mannerism.name: Mannerism
mannerism.description: After the great masters, painters bend the rules on purpose: long bodies, twisting poses, acid colors. Style itself becomes the subject.

baroque.name: Baroque
baroque.description: Art sets out to move the viewer. Strong contrasts of light and dark, bodies in motion and theatrical staging pull you into the scene.

siecledor.name: Dutch Golden Age
siecledor.description: In the prosperous Dutch Republic, artists paint for middle-class homes: quiet interiors, portraits, still lifes. Light becomes the real subject.

rococo.name: Rococo & 18th Century
rococo.description: In eighteenth-century salons, painting turns playful and intimate: garden parties, portraits, soft colors. At the same time, a few artists look quietly at ordinary life.

neoclassicism.name: Neoclassicism
neoclassicism.description: Inspired by the ruins of Rome and Pompeii, artists return to sober drawing and heroic subjects. Painting is meant to teach as much as to please.

romanticism.name: Romanticism
romanticism.description: Feeling takes over from reason. Storms, ruins, revolts and lonely figures express what the artist feels in front of a world too large to master.

ukiyoe.name: Ukiyo-e
ukiyoe.description: In Japan, woodblock prints made in series show actors, landscapes and scenes of daily life. Their flat colors and bold crops would shake up European painters.

east_asian.name: Chinese & Japanese Painting
east_asian.description: In China and Japan, painters work with brush and ink on silk, paper and folding screens. A few strokes and a lot of empty space are enough to suggest a mountain or a season.

realism.name: Realism
realism.summary: Ordinary people, painted as they are
realism.description: Painters turn away from heroes and myths to show peasants, workers and modern life, without flattering them. Showing the truth becomes a statement in itself.

american.name: American Painting
american.summary: A new country looks at itself
american.description: From portraits of the young republic to vast landscapes and scenes of city life, American painters search for subjects, and a light, of their own.

preraphaelite.name: Pre-Raphaelites & Victorian
preraphaelite.description: In Victorian Britain, a group of young painters rejects academic recipes. They paint legends and poems with intense color and almost obsessive precision.

academic.name: Academic Art
academic.summary: The polished art of the official Salon
academic.description: Trained in the great art schools, these painters master anatomy, history and a perfectly smooth finish. They were the stars of their time, before the avant-garde eclipsed them.

impressionnisme.name: Impressionism
impressionnisme.summary: Painting the light of the moment
impressionnisme.description: A group of painters leaves the studio to work outdoors, in quick little strokes. They are no longer after detail, but after the effect of light at a precise moment.

neo_impressionism.name: Neo-Impressionism
neo_impressionism.description: Painters apply science to color: small dots of pure paint, placed side by side, blend in the eye of the viewer. The picture is built slowly, like a mosaic.

postimp.name: Post-Impressionism
postimp.description: After Impressionism, everyone looks for their own path. Color no longer imitates reality: it expresses what the painter feels.

symbolism.name: Symbolism
symbolism.description: Rather than describe the visible world, these artists suggest ideas, dreams and fears. Their pictures are meant to be felt before they are understood.

secession.name: Art Nouveau & Vienna Secession
secession.description: In Vienna, young artists break with the academy. They blend painting, decoration and craft, and turn ornament into a language of its own.

fauvism.name: Fauvism
fauvism.summary: Pure color, straight from the tube
fauvism.description: For a few explosive years, painters use violent, unnatural colors and loose brushwork. Critics called them wild beasts, and the name stuck.

expressionism.name: Expressionism
expressionism.description: Artists twist shapes and push colors to express anxiety, desire or revolt. What matters is not what the world looks like, but how it feels.

cubism.name: Cubism
cubism.summary: Objects seen from several sides at once
cubism.description: Painters break objects into facets and show them from several angles in the same picture. Five centuries of perspective are suddenly called into question.

futurism.name: Futurism
futurism.summary: Speed, machines and the modern city
futurism.description: Italian artists celebrate cars, crowds and electricity. They try to paint movement itself by repeating and fragmenting forms.

abstraction.name: Abstraction & Avant-Garde
abstraction.description: Lines, shapes and colors no longer represent anything: they are the picture. Artists look for a visual language as direct as music.

dada_surrealism.name: Dada & Early Surrealism
dada_surrealism.description: Born from disgust at the First World War, Dada mocks art itself. Surrealism follows and explores dreams, chance and the unconscious.

world.name: Africa, Asia & the Americas
world.description: Bronzes, masks, stone giants and ritual objects from Africa, Asia and the Americas. They were made for ceremonies, temples and kings, long before museums existed.
